claims.text: East Marginal Way South & 1st Avenue South had 13 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are East Marginal Way South & 1st Avenue South's own: the city's record places 117 of the 163 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $890,000 a year.
48% of crashes here happened on a wet or icy road, against 19% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 0.7 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $242,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 1st Avenue South (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
The Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT) (route designation only; confirm ownership) is responsible for East Marginal Way South (signed route in OpenStreetMap; owner not confirmed).

A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) and the Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT) (route designation only; confirm ownership) is ready to draft from these facts.
